question: After safely whitening the ordered sequence/channel readout, do an explicit coarse-to-fine SNR clock, a matched flow-target loss allocation, or their interaction improve generative modeling?

source.storage: float16 transformed coordinates with a serialized exact linear inverse to the unchanged physical v27 decoder

frozen_transform.clean_coordinate_policy: mean-unit-power whitened cache; no per-token magnitude rescaling after cache construction

identification.whitening_effect: common_uniform versus unwhitened external baseline; checkpoint-level rather than perfect cache-internal causality because the representation changes
identification.interaction: ordered_weighted relative to the three other whitened arms

evaluation.advance_to_10000: advance an arm if it improves its relevant factorial control, lies within two FID, or FID/KID disagree
evaluation.early_reject: a concordant FID loss greater than two against the relevant exact-cache control can stop at 5k
evaluation.replication: a concordant 10k improvement of at least two FID with lower KID is required before another prior or tokenizer seed
nonselectors: reconstruction quality within the already-passed health envelope

orchestration: Build the one cache under supervisor and gpu-claim, validate its inverse, then start four independent supervisor-owned train-plus-5k-evaluation chains through gpu-claim. No raw CUDA launch is permitted.

launch.state: The cache and all four train-plus-FID5k chains completed under gpu-claim.

result.verdict: Reject cap-16 whitening for selection. Ordered timing recovers 38.21 FID relative to whitened common/uniform but remains 23.58 FID behind unwhitened v27. Weighting helps common time by 4.89 FID and hurts ordered time by 3.67 FID.
